topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: Introduction: Setting the Challenge
lecture_lines: Connect points A and B with a straight line.
A particle slides along a curve under gravity.
Which path reaches point B the fastest?
Straight lines aren't always the fastest path.
animations: Display the problem statement text at the center in #FFFFFF.
Show a steel ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] at the top of an incline [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/incline.svg].

Animate the ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] rolling down the incline [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/incline.svg] to highlight the path.

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: Kinetic vs. Potential Energy
lecture_lines: Gravity converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
Steeper descents yield higher speeds earlier.
This speed boost helps traverse the later path.
animations: Freeze [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] state at the bottom to compare energy levels.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Solution: The Cycloid
lecture_lines: The Brachistochrone solution is a cycloid.
Trace a point on a rolling circle.
It balances speed gain and distance reduction.
The cycloid curve is mathematically optimal.
Geometry holds the key to the fastest time.
animations: Trace a point on a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg] as it rotates along a line.
Form the cycloid path connecting two points in #FFFFFF using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg].
Flash the cycloid path to emphasize the optimal shape generated by the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg].

sections.title: Conceptual Proof: Snell’s Law Analogy
lecture_lines: Light follows the path of least time.
Gravity acts like a variable medium.
Particle speed matches light in refraction.
animations: Show layers of varying media speed #FFFF00 for light using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/flashlight.svg].
Display refraction angles bending the path of light through a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg].
Draw the parallel between light path and particle path using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-World Significance
lecture_lines: Shortest distance is not shortest time.
Calculus of variations finds this optimal path.
These principles drive modern engineering design.
animations: Animate the brachistochrone curve across the screen.
